title: SEVEN SPECIES, ONE ATMOSPHERE
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE CITY THAT COULD NOT SHARE A SECOND
candidates.premise: A coastal city survives by routing storms through an orbital weather lattice, but three districts built by different civilizations measure time with incompatible physical standards. Their control systems now issue mutually valid commands a fraction of a second apart, turning every correction into a larger cyclone while each district refuses to surrender its clock and political autonomy.

candidates.title: THE PEACE TREATY WRITTEN IN ORBITS
candidates.premise: Two moons have ended a century-long war, yet their automated defense constellations interpret routine orbital corrections as preparations for a first strike. Neither government can disarm first, and a conjunction in eighteen hours will make both networks fire without human authorization.

candidates.title: WHEN THE DEAD STAR KNOCKED
candidates.premise: A neutron star expelled from a shattered system will pass close enough to sterilize the inhabited worlds of the Ilyr. Their only workable deflection would send it centuries later through the nursery system of a younger species that cannot yet answer them.

candidates.title: THE LIBRARY THAT VOTED TO BURN
candidates.premise: A living archive containing the last medical knowledge of twelve refugee peoples votes to destroy itself after rulers repeatedly mine its memories for interrogation and war. The refugees need its cures before a seasonal plague arrives, while the archive insists that survival as an instrument is not survival.

candidates.title: SEVEN SPECIES, ONE ATMOSPHERE
candidates.premise: Seven delegations arrive at humanity's first interspecies station, only to learn that trace gases harmless to six are lethal to the seventh and that the station cannot maintain seven sealed biospheres through the approaching debris storm. A majority vote would save more bodies by sacrificing the smallest delegation.

candidates.title: THE WAR OF THE UNTRANSLATABLE PROMISE
candidates.premise: Humans and the Keth have translated each other's words but not the structure of commitment. Humans treat a promise as an obligation held by a continuing person; Keth identities branch and recombine, so they recognize only probabilistic duties held by a lineage. Each side therefore reads the other's sincere treaty as deliberate fraud, and border fleets are mobilizing.

candidates.title: THE PLANET INSIDE THE STORM
candidates.premise: Settlers on a gas giant's floating cities use weather engines to keep their habitats aloft. The engines unknowingly sever the migration paths of an indigenous aerial biosphere whose continent-sized organisms generate the very updrafts the cities need. Turning the engines off drops the cities; leaving them on drives the biosphere to extinction and guarantees a later collapse.

candidates.title: THE LAST BRIDGE BETWEEN UNIVERSES
candidates.premise: A bridge between two universes is failing as their physical constants drift apart. Closing it strands nine million migrants whose bodies now depend on medicines from their universe of origin; keeping it fully open begins to unravel causality around cities on both sides.

candidates.title: A COURT FOR THE FUTURE THAT CANNOT SPEAK
candidates.premise: A frozen colony must release geothermal heat to survive its next winter, but the same heat will awaken an engineered intelligence distributed through the planet's ocean. Models disagree on whether awakening now will nurture a new person or irreversibly damage a mind not ready to form.

candidates.title: THE HOUSE THAT REMEMBERED EVERY TENANT
candidates.premise: An old communal house has become sentient from generations of accumulated memories. Its foundations are failing above a crowded transit tunnel, but it refuses demolition because its rooms understand destruction as the death of everyone they remember; current residents refuse evacuation because developers will erase both their homes and the house's testimony.

selection.title: SEVEN SPECIES, ONE ATMOSPHERE
selection.reason: The conflict is hard and external, with seven strong parties and a built-in moral trap: a majority vote that sacrifices the smallest delegation looks rational. The solution (tolerance curves over time instead of seven fixed atmospheres) is visible, testable and can be surprising beforehand and obvious afterward. Every delegation keeps a veto, and the smallest species ends up setting the safety floor. It also differs from the two recent Dailies: a closed room under a clock, not an orbital corridor and not a conversation with a star. Close runners-up: 6 (untranslatable promise: deepest conceptual intelligence, but at risk of exposition) and 2 (orbital treaty: strong clock, but too close to the Oct 5 orbital corridor).
selection.risk: The pulsed-gas / rotating-occupancy design could read as a convenient engineering fix explained by Illuminara rather than found by her. The author must show her measuring, testing a wrong first model, and being corrected by a delegation's own expertise, and must give a real objection to the final route.

rounds.summary: Claude selected the seven-species station crisis for its hard external stakes, sympathetic majority logic, testable time-axis solution and preserved veto power, while warning that the mechanism had to be discovered in scenes rather than merely explained.
GPT drafted a six-part rescue procedural in which Illuminara reframed seven fixed atmospheres as survival intervals and combined physical reinforcement with shared control of the air.

Claude found the premise and outcome strong but asked for explicit power arithmetic, dramatized discovery, a real failed model, an exercised veto and a clearly planted destination for the final structural load.
GPT made the power and cell arithmetic explicit, staged the bound-halene failure, let Daro co-design and exercise local latches, and planted the empty docking spine before the impact.

Claude found the revision close to final and requested only two small continuity repairs: suspend the detachment order for the live trial and clarify that the final clock measured the twelve-minute impact window.
GPT made the two narrow continuity repairs, preserved the mechanism and outcome, and kept the Vey-last authorization, Daro’s refusal and the credible costs intact.
Claude closed the exact final as complete, canon-safe and public-safe with no hard blockers, confirming that all 819 lives were saved and no species retained a master hand over the shared air.

final_critic_line: Seven species, one failing atmosphere: Illuminara reframes survival as intervals in time, builds a route that needs no single master hand, and every life aboard is kept.

evaluation.note: Retrospective fixed-anchor SA1, two real independent ratings per model, model means weighted equally; classes not calibrated to agree.
